title: Australia’s cash splash in Solomons will cost more than it delivers
gist: Australia's almost $1 billion security-treaty package for Solomon Islands reportedly includes $93 million over three years routed to each of the 50 MPs' constituencies — a move the author argues entrenches the corruption-prone Constituency Development Fund patronage system Canberra long tried to reform, plays into opposition leader Sogavare's hands and risks compromising reformist PM Matthew Wale. The $142 million for free education and visa access are more defensible.

insights.claim: A text from Australia's High Commissioner Jeffrey Roach to Solomons Deputy PM Francis Sade, verified by the ABC, outlined a plan giving every Solomon Islands MP access to almost $2 million in Australian aid over three years for constituency 'development priorities' — $93 million in total — as part of an almost $1 billion treaty incentive package.
